environment.hypervisor: Proxmox VE 9 on a Dell R530 lab server (Intel Xeon E5-2620 v4), VMs 505 (source) and 506 (restore), destroyed after the run
environment.vm: fresh Debian 13.7 genericcloud amd64 image 20261116-2664 (sha256 edd2b3fb9de8bc51b29ff8425716180c8f631f23f6b07f9e288a57bd18701116), x86_64, 2 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM, 16 GiB disk
environment.install_method: Debian packages built natively on a separate Debian 13 VM with kanidm_ppa_automation d5327e7 (build_native.sh + build_debs.sh, rust 1.96.1, cargo-deb 2.11.2); apt-get install of the two local .deb files; packaged systemd unit kanidmd.service (Type=notify, DynamicUser=yes)
environment.domain: idm.onemind.test (origin https://idm.onemind.test:8443), the same on both boxes
environment.tls: local test CA from kanidmd cert-generate
environment.authenticator: software virtual WebAuthn authenticator (tools/aklab.py SoftPasskey: P-256, none attestation, UP+UV flags); not a phone, security key or browser virtual authenticator

rehearsal: the scripts were debugged first on a separate VM (508, destroyed): a setup bug (cert-generate before the state directory existed) and client fixes (MFA required for persons, gateway read group, OIDC scope per group, TOTP step handling, restore timing). See rehearsal-attempt-0-AK-1.txt. The counted run used two VMs created fresh from the cloud image.

AK-1.facts: enabled + active after systemctl reboot (boot_id changed, NRestarts=0), /status true, healthcheck ok, no k3s or container units/binaries

AK-2.facts: booted with Proxmox link_down=1, eth0 also set down in the guest, no route and no DNS; idm_admin recovered, owner created, passkey enrolled and owner signed in with it, all through the QEMU guest agent with no network
AK-2.note: kanidmd became active 2 min 9 s after boot when offline (unit waits for network-online.target)

AK-3.facts: four onemind_* groups, one person in each, memberof read over REST by a service-account API token (needs membership of idm_account_mail_read)

AK-4.facts: auth code + PKCE S256; ES256 ID token signature verified against the client JWKS; claim onemind_role = owner/adult/child per group; scope maps differ (owners get email, adults profile, children only openid groups; a child asking for profile is refused); guest (no mapped group) refused with 403

AK-5.facts: reset link used to enrol password + TOTP for child1, sign-in with it works, second use of the same link refused (401 sessionexpired)

AK-6.facts: guest signed in before expiry; 30 s after expiry sign-in denied ('account expired') and the earlier session token refused (401 on /v1/self and /v1/auth/valid)

AK-7.facts: online backup written by the running server (scheduled, PID unchanged, /status true); restored on fresh VM 506 with the same domain; the same owner passkey (credential fingerprint 58d340207caabd97, enrolled in AK-2) signed in

AK-8.facts: the same TOTP code was accepted twice within one 30 s step (both passwordmfa sign-ins succeeded)
AK-8.source: kanidm v1.12.0 server/lib/src/credential/totp.rs Totp::verify (line 246) accepts the current and previous step with no record of used codes; server/lib/src/idm/authsession/mod.rs lines 512-518 call it with no replay check

AK-10.facts: adult1 got an ID token, was removed from onemind_adults, and the next OIDC authorise was refused with 403

verdict_reason: AK-1 to AK-7 and AK-10 PASS in one run on fresh machines; AK-8 FAILS (Kanidm v1.12.0 TOTP has no replay protection). Per the README rule this goes to the founder; the identity provider is not switched (BD-03, D-015).
